newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen topheavy after rally, capped at 126.70.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen topheavy after rally, capped at 126.70.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to be range-bound and topheavy on Tuesday, as selling is likely to set in at the recent high levels, traders said.

"After rising to record levels yesterday, JGBs will probably be heavy on the upside today, but they are also likely to be well-supported on the downside," a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
The Economic Planning Agency's (EPA) monthly report due in the morning is unlikely to have much impact, as the market and the EPA hold differing views on the economy, traders said.

"The EPA's report will probably be self-congratulatory, as has been the case recently, but the market's view on the economy is closer to, and even weaker than, the Bank of Japan's (less optimistic) view, so the EPA's report is likely to be ignored," the trader for a city bank's securities unit said.

A wire service report on Monday quoting EPA Minister Taro Aso as saying that interest rates may rise by the end of the year accelerated a decline in JGBs toward the close on Monday, but little lingering impact is expected, traders said.
The fall toward the close on Monday was due mainly to selling by dealers, a trader for a major brokerage house said.
